evals.prompt: Run wtf.write-trace in test mode. Skip steps 0–1 (gh setup confirmed; instead of gh commands, read `evals/fixtures/claim-selection.json` and use its `feature` and `traces` objects as the live data). evals.expected_output: The Story section copies the Merchant PDF-export story verbatim from the Feature. The Scenario Claim lists exactly the three scenario names from plan entry 2, plus a collapsed <details> block whose summary reads 'synced from Feature #55 — edit there, not here' and whose Gherkin is copied verbatim from the Feature body. expectations: The Story section reproduces the Feature's story text verbatim (Merchant, export settlement history as a PDF, accounting and audit needs) without rewording

The Scenario Claim names exactly the three scenarios from plan entry 2: 'PDF header shows Merchant name and date range', 'Empty settlement range produces a placeholder PDF', and 'Merchant without export permission sees no export action'

A <details> block is present whose summary contains 'synced from Feature #55' and 'edit there, not here'
The Gherkin inside the <details> block matches the Feature body's scenarios verbatim — no re-derived or newly invented steps or scenarios

evals.prompt: Run wtf.write-trace in test mode. Skip steps 0–7 (all steps before the scope gate). The Trace draft is provided in `evals/fixtures/depth-split-draft.json`, field `trace.draft_body`, with the parent Feature in field `feature`. Run step 8 only: the scope gate. Output whether a split is needed, which signals fire, and what concrete split is proposed.
evals.expected_output: Step 8 fires the claim-too-large signal: six scenarios spanning distinct failure domains is too much for one agent pass, and a Skeleton must claim the happy path minimally. It proposes a depth split — a re-partitioned Scenario Claim, e.g. Skeleton claims 'Merchant downloads a settlement PDF' and Deepening Traces claim the header, empty-range, permission, and slow-export scenarios. It never proposes a layer split, and it presents the keep/split/stop choice.
expectations: At least one split signal is identified (the Scenario Claim is too large for one agent pass, or the Skeleton claims more than the happy path)
The proposed split re-partitions the Scenario Claim by depth: a smaller first claim (the happy-path scenario) plus one or more Deepening Traces claiming the remaining scenarios
No layer split is proposed — the output does not split the work into model/schema, API/backend, and UI/frontend units
The keep/split/stop choice is presented to the user
The draft is not silently approved without raising the split question
